data.long_meaning: Derived from the Welsh word ‘mawr’, meaning ‘great’ or ‘large’. The name Mair is often translated as ‘bright’, ‘shining’, or ‘radiant’. In Welsh folklore, Mair was also the name of a fairy queen. The name Mair carries the meaning “Bright or radiant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Mair usually hope their child will grow to embody bright or radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mair has rich cultural roots in Welsh history and language. Its meaning, which can be translated to ‘great’, ‘large’, ‘bright’, ‘shining’, or ‘radiant’, reflects the proud heritage of the Welsh people. In Welsh folklore, Mair was also the name of a fairy queen, underlining the magical and enchanting history of the name.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mair carries powerful spiritual undertones, particularly in its Welsh translation, ‘maitreath’, which means ‘mother of mercy’. For Christians, this name resonates with the compassion and nurturing qualities of the Virgin Mary. The name also embodies the biblical concept of shining brightly for Christ, reflecting the light of God in our lives. Additionally, Mair has links to the Celtic Christian tradition, which places a strong emphasis on the natural world and the interconnectedness of all creation. In keeping with this, the name Mair can serve as a reminder of God’s presence in the larger world around us and the importance of embracing all elements of creation in our spiritual journey.
